prompt: the core components of Java NIO are:
judge_reasoning: Candidate [1] best answers the prompt by correctly identifying the fundamental Java NIO components (Channels, Buffers, Selectors) and adding charset support in a way that is consistent with NIO’s architecture. Candidate [2] also covers the core triad but dilutes “core components” with extra items (e.g., Locks) and includes some misleading claims (e.g., about channels transferring directly between buffers and an unsupported “most common” buffer type). Candidate [3] is largely inaccurate, introducing non-existent/incorrectly framed items such as “AsyncChannels” and “BlockingQueue Channels,” and adding many non-core features. Candidate [4] contains multiple clear factual errors (e.g., wrong claims about channel read/write capabilities, ByteBuffer storing only text, selectors not being part of NIO, and Path utilities being read-only only).
